sessionName: Week 3 - Getting in before the tender
summary: George Berrington led a demand generation session with Andrew Fenwick and Kate Rowley focused on reaching buyers before tenders are published. Elmstead currently has no outbound activity and relies on tender portals. We agreed a partner-led outbound programme into named change directors and a small roundtable series, with tender portal monitoring kept but deprioritised.

discussion.keyPoints: Kate confirmed almost all opportunities come from tender portal alerts and two frameworks. There is no outbound and the website gets about 300 visits a month.
Andrew noted that many public bodies run pre-market engagement events six to nine months before a tender. Elmstead rarely attends them. George suggested treating these as a primary channel.
Kate worried partners will not find time for outbound. Andrew agreed to ring-fence half a day a week for each of the five partners.

recommendations.recommendation: Shift effort to 50 percent outbound and pre-market engagement, 30 percent frameworks and 20 percent open tenders over the next two quarters.
Each of the five partners to run a named list of 25 change directors, with half a day a week ring-fenced for outreach.
Run a quarterly roundtable in Leeds for water utility change directors, capped at 12 attendees.
Use a six-touch sequence over 30 days mixing LinkedIn, email and a phone call from the partner.
Track pre-tender conversations as the lead metric, targeting 20 per quarter, rather than tender alerts received.

actions.action: Build partner target lists of 25 change directors each
Book every pre-market engagement event in the water and NHS calendars for the next six months

nextFocus: Sharpen discovery and qualification so partners turn pre-tender conversations into shaped opportunities.
nextPreparation: Kate to bring the current bid/no-bid checklist and two recent proposals.

tests.question: What channel mix split did we agree?
